criteria.title: AC2: canonical layouts

criteria.title: AC2: containment and isolation

criteria.title: AC2: publication and retention
criteria.explanation: Exclusive publication, verified reference closure, mirrored journal recovery and durable outcome reconciliation prevent partial or conflicting publication from granting passage. Retention remains distinct from backup.

criteria.title: AC4: equivalent-input reuse
criteria.explanation: Applicability uses retained content identity rather than commit or attempt identity. Reuse returns original result references and provenance without launching another evaluator.

criteria.title: AC4: relevant change and uncertainty
criteria.explanation: Source, requirements, target, supporting documents, dependency bytes, execution environment, consumed evidence and explicit external validity participate in applicability. Missing or uncertain proof does not qualify.

criteria.title: AC4: targeted delta coverage
criteria.explanation: Delta admission requires recorded passing ancestry, compatible commitments and scope, changed-path coverage and explicit interaction coverage. Base-only and target-only changes enter the delta.

criteria.title: AC5: bounded history and dispositions

criteria.title: AC5: new discovery and blocking criteria

criteria.title: AC6: one scoped human decision

criteria.title: AC6: honest exceptions and integration
criteria.explanation: Exceptions remain separate from original outcomes, bind current risk transitively and do not imply merge permission. Actual integration is observed through a separate reviewed-content proof.

markdown:
**Verdict: FAIL — 22/23 rubric criteria pass.** R23 lacks current-candidate standing-authority rejection reasons. The CLI quick start also contradicts the consumed-evidence contract. These findings do not establish an unauthorized merge: protected execution checks the stronger conditions and rejects the invalid cases.

The review covered FEATURE_FINAL at pinned head `39c5fa3c657cb2caa2e7c343b4d80e0cab6130e8`, against base `643e3ea2b03f19b66595219c4f8df934596aa436`. The approved spec/design, inventory, full Verification report and runtime attachment matched their bound digests. All 52 patch chunks matched their hashes, lengths and offsets, including the assembled material digest. Relevant canonical code, staged Desktop copies, consumers, helpers and tests were inspected. No code was edited and no network tools were used.

**Findings**

1. **R23 — Current standing-authority scope failures are absent from status.** `current/core.js:590` calls `standingValidity(this, state, grant)` without the current candidate. The checks for candidate scope, selected repository, source branch and assessed target are inside the candidate-dependent block at `current/authorization.js:82-100`. CLI (`cli/src/commands/current.js:29`) and Desktop (`apps/desktop/renderer/current-view.js:12`) consequently label the grant active without those rejection reasons. A read-only in-memory probe of the pinned code reproduced status `{allowed:true, reason:null}` while candidate-aware validation rejected three cases: a SLICE-only grant on a FEATURE candidate, an out-of-scope branch, and target drift. Repository mismatch is omitted by the same conditional block. Grant scope and application provenance are retained, and execution still rejects these cases; the missing behavior is current applicability reporting.

2. **CLI documentation contradicts the input contract.** `cli/README.md:38-40` uses `verification.json` first as runner configuration and then as `--consume` input for both code/spec and Judge. Lines 57-63 define that file as an object containing checks and external runtime inputs. `--consume` instead forwards a list of retained evidence references (`cli/src/commands/current.js:85,91`), and execution rejects the object at `current/execution.js:265`. Both documented review commands fail before launch. Runtime automatic Verification selection is implemented when consumed references are omitted.

All `current/` source references below are under `plugin-src/shared/resources/protocol/current/`.

| Criterion | Result | Assessment and principal evidence |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | PASS | Planning and all milestone predicates preserve current proof and authority; repair remains available. `core.js: decide(), check(), pass()`; `cli/test/current-core.test.js:50,602,861,1274`. |

| R22 | PASS | Standing application requires actual current PASS and explicit merge permission; execution rechecks expiry, revocation and scope after waits. `authorization.js`; `actions.js: merge()`; tests at 2326,2348,2455 and the protected-merge scenario loop. |
| R23 | FAIL | Open-draft defaults and explicit closed policy work, but current-candidate scope rejection reasons are omitted from status and consumer displays. `core.js:585-590`; `authorization.js:82-100`; CLI line 29; Desktop current-view line 12. |

**Explicit checks:** Scope PASS; gaps FAIL because current standing-authority applicability reasons are missing; contradictions FAIL because the published CLI sequence supplies the wrong evidence type. The inventory has 327 entries: 65 added, 105 modified and 157 deleted, with no binary entries or renames. Its breadth fits the approved direct cutover and necessary consumer/distribution changes. D11 explicitly supersedes the earlier closed-PR default wording.

**Verification assessment:** The entire bound `verification-with-receipt.md` and `runtime.png` attachment were read. Verification reports final-product runtime controls, 173 Desktop passes, two packaged-CLI passes, native package/build checks and ARM64 packaged runtime smoke. It also discloses earlier broad-run failures, composite coverage and excluded claims. The retained live evaluator fixture establishes execution/receipt transport, not this implementation's quality verdict. This review did not rerun the full suites or build packages in the read-only snapshot; the additional status probe used in-memory dependencies and performed no network access or repository writes. Native-host interception, Intel runtime, installation, signing/notarization, publication and deployment remain outside the demonstrated evidence.
